status: DRAFT for review: drafted from 'PR Creation Flow in NAM_final_version.docx' (How a Purchase Request is Created in NAM for Goods); correct it with the business owner before production use
about: The officer's journey as the PR Creation Flow describes it, laid over the harness's own stages (orchestrator.STAGES). waku/nam/journey.py reads it; nothing here decides anything. A step is done when every condition in done_when holds on the case. Conditions: record:<path> (a Need Record field is set), artifact:<name>[.<path>] (a flow left it), check:<name> (an orchestrator check passes), gate:<name> (the approval is given), action:<name> (the action is confirmed), flagged:<artifact> (a line of it carries one of the flags below); a leading ! means the opposite, and a list inside done_when holds when any one of its conditions holds. A step with no done_when is a behaviour of its stage, not a separate milestone.

phases.name: Need Identification
phases.says: The user chats with NAM to make clear what they need and to choose the exact items.

steps.name: The category
steps.says: NAM asks whether the need is goods, services or works.
steps.user: the category: goods, services or works

steps.name: The need in the user's words
steps.says: The user types the need in the NAM chat in their own words.
steps.user: the need, in their own words
steps.nam: the request as NAM read it

steps.name: Several items split
steps.says: A request with several items is split, and each item becomes its own search terms.
steps.nam: the items and their search terms

steps.name: Past purchases searched
steps.says: NAM searches the Knowledge Graph by meaning and by keyword for past purchase lines that match.
steps.nam: the similar past tenders and lines, with their source

steps.name: The missing details found
steps.says: NAM checks what is still needed to describe the item fully: size or range, material, standard, rating, certificate, quantity, date needed, location, use.
steps.nam: the follow-up questions, built from the past lines and NRL's specifications

steps.name: Follow-up questions answered
steps.says: The user clicks an option or types an answer; NAM matches it to the closest option and repeats back what it understood. An answer that does not fit gets one short clarifying question.
steps.user: an answer to each follow-up question, in everyday words
steps.nam: the answer matched to an option, or one clarifying question

steps.name: NRL's standard value when the user does not know
steps.says: If the user does not know a required detail, NAM uses NRL's standard value and marks it default, so a reviewer can see it did not come from the user.
steps.user: "I don't know" is a valid answer

steps.name: The item description is complete
steps.says: NAM stops asking once every required detail is captured and the category, procurement type and tender type are confirmed.
steps.user: confirmation of the category, procurement type and tender type

steps.name: The matching past tenders
steps.says: NAM shows the past tenders that hold the matching items, latest first: ordered and delivered, then ordered and not yet delivered, then raised and cancelled.
steps.nam: the ranked list of matching tenders

steps.name: The items picked
steps.says: The user looks at each tender's items and picks the ones needed; they become the estimate lines, one per item.
steps.user: the tender (precedent) and the items to take from it
steps.nam: the picked items, grouped into estimate lines

steps.name: The quantities finalised
steps.says: Every line gets its quantity and unit, and the officer approves the quantities.
steps.user: the quantity and unit of each line, then the quantity approval

phases.name: Estimate creation
phases.says: From the chosen items NAM works out the expected cost from the most recent purchase of those items, brought up to today.

steps.name: The last price found
steps.says: For each line NAM finds the last price paid, rate contract first, then PO; same code first, then an equivalent code; and records where it came from.
steps.nam: the last price of each line, with its source

steps.name: The price brought up to today
steps.says: NAM brings the last price up to the evaluation date at the yearly escalation in the policy, counting whole years.
steps.nam: the estimated rate of each line

steps.name: The estimate filled in
steps.says: NAM fills the estimate sheet; the user can change the quantity or the rate of any line. A line with no past price (a new item) needs its rate from the user.
steps.user: the rate of any line with no past price, and any quantity or rate change
steps.nam: the estimate table: code, description, unit, quantity, rate, amount, price source

steps.name: Each rate checked
steps.says: NAM compares each rate with the last price and gives each line a result. A flag is a warning only; NAM does not change the price by itself.

steps.name: The flagged lines decided
steps.says: Every flagged line is accepted or revised by the user; the estimate cannot be locked until each has a decision. A line with no flag needs no decision.
steps.user: accept or revise each flagged line
steps.nam: the decision log of the flagged lines

steps.name: The estimate locked
steps.says: The user checks the quantities and locks the estimate; the locked rate becomes the PR's valuation price.
steps.nam: the locked estimate and its basis per line

phases.name: PR Creation
phases.says: NAM uses everything gathered before to fill the Purchase Request and send it to SAP.

steps.name: The PR filled in
steps.says: NAM fills each PR field from the earlier stages and records where each value came from.
steps.user: the PR fields only the user knows: delivery date, plant, storage location and any other field still empty
steps.nam: the filled PR, with the source of each field

steps.name: The PR sent to SAP
steps.says: NAM checks every mandatory field, shows the PR to confirm, then posts it to SAP; SAP's PR number is linked to the need.
steps.nam: the SAP PR number, linked to the need

flags.AHR: the rate rose more than the yearly limit since the last price
flags.manual_review: the rate rose by the limit or more and the last price is less than a year old
